oneFilter.intro: Before I say yes to anything, or pick what to work on, run it through this:
questions: Does it move D-One toward autonomous? (Client's + contractor's favourite subcontractor · interchangeable humans · Darren out one month at a time.) Or is it just chase-mode?
Is it the current bottleneck? (Growth Wheel.) Or a shiny distraction from the real constraint?
Do I have capacity? I am a basket — rest fills it, output empties it. Am I resting as much as I'm outputting? Am I inside my 20% buffer?
If it's a deal: Is it what we actually want, and do we hold the power seat? The one willing to walk away has the most power.

Is this slot actually free? A blank space is not automatically free — before I say yes, check the board for what else could have gone there (surf, rest, family, focus). Every yes is a no to something else.

active.context: Darren and Amanda are in a really positive place. Pattern to shift: Darren tends to go straight to wanting intimacy without first building the emotional foundation Amanda needs to feel open, desired, and attracted. Katie is helping Darren figure out the specific work needed to consistently build Amanda up day-to-day (not just when he wants intimacy) so she feels seen and wanted on her own terms. Amanda is fully on board with this. Goal: show up consistently in a way that works for both of them. Key insight (2026-08-29): for Darren, closeness is often counterintuitive — leaning in / being close and present can actually smother Amanda, whereas genuinely creating space is what builds real connection for her. The distinction that matters is whether the space is generous (secure, trusting, living his own life well) versus withholding (a tactic to make her chase) — genuine space reads as security, strategic space reads as a game. notes: Zone of Genius (what I most love, what makes me lose track of time): collaborating, creating, starting, igniting, developing, building.

What work doesn't feel like work: new client pitches/vision-casting, building D1Brain itself, EO Learning Chair facilitation, partnership/brand conversations, kicking off a new project. Common thread = anything at the front end of something new.

The tension: my zone of genius is starting/igniting things, but the owner-not-operator goal requires the parts of D-One that DON'T feel like flow (maintaining, chasing, reconciling, monitoring) to run without me — those need systems/people, not more of my attention.
Open question to keep working: what's the one ops/admin thing on my plate right now that could move off me this month, and who owns it (Amanda/Caren/Stafford/Berna)?

Unique Ability: people and relationships — connecting and relating, translating into others' language, seeing and understanding their perspective (and multiple perspectives at once), distilling into simple terms, seeing patterns, seeing the bigger picture, seeing clarity through complexity.
